q: Does the ALDH+ / f_s correspondence generalize to other cancer-stem-cell markers (CD44+, CD133+, side-population)?
basis: The Fukui et al. IMK model treats f_s as a scalar 'stem-cell fraction' anchored to ALDH+ flow measurements, and the 4/4 agreement within 1 sigma (claim A) is impressive. But ALDH activity is a metabolic assay (aldefluor), not a lineage marker, and ALDH+ overlaps only partially with CD44+/CD133+ in oral squamous carcinoma. The IMK derivation nowhere requires the marker be ALDH specifically; the same fit could in principle be done with any stem-like subpopulation.
next_steps: Refit the IMK model against published CD44+/CD133+/side-population sort + clonogenic data for the same or comparable oral SCC lines (SAS, HSC-2, CAL-27). Compare f_s posteriors marker-by-marker. If f_s is marker-invariant, the model captures a true biological subpopulation; if it is marker-dependent, f_s is a phenomenological knob and the paper's causal ALDH -> radioresistance claim weakens. Also test whether joint ALDH+/CD44+ double-positive gives an even tighter fit.

q: Can the phenomenological (a+c) SLDR rate be replaced by an explicit repair-pathway model (NHEJ + HR + MMEJ kinetics) without losing fit quality?
basis: In the Fukui model, (a+c) is a single lumped repair-rate parameter (units 1/h), with reported values ~1.3-2.8 1/h. Modern DNA-damage-response models (MEDRAS, LEM-IV, McMahon-Prise 2016) decompose double-strand-break repair into distinct pathways with cell-cycle-dependent kinetics. It is currently unclear whether the ~2x w_SLDR increase in HSC2-R reflects a genuinely upregulated repair pathway or is degeneracy in a lumped-parameter fit.
next_steps: Wire the IMK's SLDR term into a two-pathway repair model (fast NHEJ + slow HR) using pathway rates from Reynolds et al. 2012 (MRE11 / RAD51 foci) or MEDRAS defaults. Refit against Fig 5 + Fig 6 data. Compare AIC/BIC vs the lumped (a+c). If the two-pathway model wins, decompose the SAS-R vs SAS w_SLDR increase into NHEJ-fold-change vs HR-fold-change. Cross-reference with any RAD51/53BP1 foci data for these cell lines.

q: How sensitive is the fit to the operational definition of 'ALDH+' (aldefluor gate percentile, DEAB control stringency, flow-gating strategy)?
basis: Fig 3 reports ALDH+ percentages of 0.97 +/- 0.68% (SAS) up to 12.61 +/- 6.11% (HSC2-R). These are aldefluor-assay percentages that depend heavily on where the DEAB-inhibited negative gate is drawn (top 0.5% vs top 1% vs top 2% of aldefluor signal are all defensible choices). The reported error bars (roughly +/- 50%) show substantial sensitivity to gating; refits of f_s inherit this uncertainty. It is not clear whether the impressive 4/4 agreement in claim A would hold under a stricter or looser gate.
next_steps: Reprocess the Fig 3 flow data (if released or if comparable FCS files exist in cellxgene / FlowRepository) under three gating protocols: (a) fixed 1% DEAB threshold, (b) 2-sigma-above-DEAB-mean, (c) automated GMM. Rerun IMK MCMC with each ALDH+ prior. Report f_s posterior shift per gating choice. If f_s posteriors are within 1 sigma across all three gates, robustness is confirmed; if not, quote the gating-uncertainty envelope explicitly.

q: Do the model's predictions transfer to other tumor types (glioblastoma, head-and-neck adenocarcinoma, breast) that also show ALDH+/radioresistance correlation?
basis: The paper is scoped to oral squamous carcinoma (SAS, HSC-2 families). Meanwhile, ALDH+ radioresistance has been reported in GBM (Bao et al.), breast (Ginestier), and colon (Huang) stem-like populations, with different baseline ALDH+ fractions and radiosensitivity profiles. It is an open question whether the IMK + f_s formalism is a universal model or an oral-SCC-specific fit; the w_SLDR ~ 1.9 for HSC2-R is not obviously predicted by any general theory.
next_steps: Assemble a small cross-tumor dataset (5-8 published cell-line pairs: parental + radioresistant sub-line) covering GBM (U87, U251), breast (MCF-7, MDA-MB-231), and pancreatic (Panc-1). Extract acute-dose survival + ALDH+ % from published figures. Refit the IMK model globally with a shared alpha_0, beta_0, (a+c) baseline and per-tumor-type offset. Test whether w_SLDR clusters by tissue or by baseline ALDH+ fraction. Report on cross-tumor predictive utility.

q: Can radiosensitivity (alpha_0, beta_0, w_SLDR) be predicted from transcriptomic ALDH-isoform expression alone, obviating the need for wet-lab clonogenic assays?
basis: The paper's IMK fit requires 3+ days of clonogenic-assay work per cell line to constrain alpha_0, beta_0, (a+c), and f_s. If ALDH isoform expression (ALDH1A1, ALDH1A3, ALDH3A1) from a single RNA-seq measurement correlated well with fit parameters, the model could be used prospectively on patient tumor biopsies without wet-lab radiobiology. Depmap has RNA-seq + radiation-response for many of these lines.
next_steps: Pull Depmap CCLE RNA-seq for oral-SCC lines (SAS, HSC-2, CAL-27, HSC-3, HSC-4, Ca9-22 etc.) plus their reported clonogenic alpha/beta if available. Train a leave-one-out ridge regression: log(w_SLDR) ~ ALDH1A1 + ALDH1A3 + ALDH3A1 + BRCA1 + RAD51 + XRCC5. Report cross-validated MSE and shapley values for each gene. If ALDH isoforms dominate, this validates the paper's mechanistic claim; if repair genes dominate, w_SLDR is really a repair-machinery readout. Extend to TCGA HNSC patient data as a second validation cohort.
